topical.text: Ceramide-rich emollients BID · Topical steroid (potency matched to site) · Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus 0.1%, pimecrolimus 1%) · Crisaborole (PDE4 inhibitor) · Ruxolitinib cream 1.5% (JAK1/2, age ≥12)
topical.detail: Emollients: Foundation of all AD therapy; apply within 3 minutes of bathing (soak-and-smear). Topical steroids: match potency to body site — avoid high-potency on face, axillae, groin. TCIs (tacrolimus/pimecrolimus): steroid-sparing for sensitive areas; FDA black-box (rare lymphoma risk historically debated). Crisaborole 2%: non-steroidal PDE4 inhibitor; effective for mild-moderate AD (age ≥2). Ruxolitinib cream: rapid itch relief (within 36h in trials); approved for mild-moderate AD age ≥12. PMID 29385376.

systemic-nonimmune.text: Sedating H1 antihistamines at bedtime (hydroxyzine, diphenhydramine) for sleep disruption · Non-sedating H1 (fexofenadine, cetirizine) — limited efficacy in AD
systemic-nonimmune.detail: Antihistamines have limited direct anti-pruritic efficacy in AD (itch is not primarily histamine-mediated in AD). Sedating antihistamines (hydroxyzine 25-50mg QHS) are used for sleep disruption only. Caution in elderly (anticholinergic effects, fall risk).

systemic-targeted.text: Dupilumab (IL-4Rα mAb) — primary biologic · Tralokinumab (IL-13 mAb) · Lebrikizumab (IL-13 mAb) · JAK inhibitors: upadacitinib (JAK1) or abrocitinib (JAK1) for moderate-severe
systemic-targeted.detail: Dupilumab: IL-4/IL-13 dual blockade; fastest onset for pruritus among AD biologics; SQ Q2W; approved age ≥6 months for moderate-severe AD. Tralokinumab: IL-13 selective; SQ Q2W (QW induction); approved adults. JAK1 inhibitors: Upadacitinib 15/30mg QD; abrocitinib 100/200mg QD; oral; superior itch reduction in head-to-head trials vs dupilumab. Screen for VTE risk, TB, viral hepatitis before JAK inhibitors. PMID 29385376.

topical.text: Cooling moisturizer / menthol-containing lotion (1% menthol in aqueous cream) · Lukewarm showers (avoid hot water) · Physical cooling vest for severe intractable itch
topical.detail: Cooling stimulates cold-sensitive TRPM8 receptors, inhibiting itch sensation at the peripheral level. Menthol 1% in emollient provides temporary relief of cholestatic itch and is well-tolerated. Avoid hot water — heat exacerbates bile acid-mediated itch. Physical cooling devices (ice packs, cooling vests) can dramatically reduce itch intensity in severe cholestatic pruritus.

systemic-nonimmune.text: Cholestyramine 4g QID (bile acid sequestrant, first-line) · Rifampin 150-300mg BID (PXR-mediated bile acid clearance) · Naltrexone 50mg QD (opioid antagonist) · Sertraline 75-100mg QD · Obeticholic acid + bezafibrate (add-on in PBC)
systemic-nonimmune.detail: Cholestyramine: Binds bile acids in the gut; take 1 hour before/4 hours after other medications (binds drugs). GI side effects common. Rifampin: PXR nuclear receptor agonist; enhances bile acid hydroxylation and excretion; monitor LFTs (hepatotoxicity in 2-13%). Naltrexone: μ-opioid receptor antagonist; endogenous opioid tone is elevated in cholestasis; start 12.5mg and titrate to avoid opioid withdrawal-like reaction. Sertraline: second-line; mechanism unclear; GI side effects limit use. PMID 29385376.

systemic-targeted.text: Linerixibat (IBAT inhibitor — Phase 3 for PBC-related itch) · Maralixibat (pediatric PFIC) · Liver transplant for intractable pruritus in liver failure (definitive)
systemic-targeted.detail: IBAT inhibitors (ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors): Block intestinal bile acid reabsorption; linerixibat in Phase 3 trials for PBC-associated pruritus. Emerging but not yet standard. Liver transplant: Definitive treatment for otherwise intractable cholestatic pruritus due to end-stage liver disease. Pruritus alone is not a listing criterion, but refractory pruritus reduces quality of life and may influence listing discussions.

topical.text: Ceramide-containing emollients BID (reduce TEWL) · Capsaicin 0.025-0.075% cream (TRPV1 desensitization) · Pramoxine 1% lotion (topical anesthetic) · Tacrolimus 0.1% ointment (localized areas)
topical.detail: Emollients: Uremic patients have impaired barrier function + xerosis; ceramide-rich formulas preferred. Capsaicin: Depletes substance P from cutaneous nerve endings; initial burning sensation limits tolerability. Begin with 0.025% and titrate. High-concentration capsaicin 8% patch (Qutenza) may be useful under specialist supervision. Pramoxine: Available in specialized CKD pruritus formulations; well-tolerated.

systemic-nonimmune.text: Gabapentin 100-300mg post-dialysis (renally dose-adjusted) · Pregabalin 25-75mg QD-BID (renally adjusted) · Optimize dialysis adequacy (Kt/V target ≥1.2) · Thalidomide 100mg QHS (third-line, refractory) · Nalfurafine (κ-opioid agonist, available Japan/Korea)
systemic-nonimmune.detail: Gabapentinoids: Reduce itch intensity and improve sleep; most evidence for gabapentin in hemodialysis. Dose after each dialysis session and reduce based on residual renal function. Monitor for dizziness, somnolence (accumulation risk in CKD). Dialysis adequacy: Increasing dialysis dose (Kt/V) or switch to high-flux membranes reduces but rarely eliminates pruritus. Thalidomide: Anti-inflammatory + immunomodulatory; significant teratogenicity risk — strict REMS program required. PMID 29385376.

systemic-targeted.text: Difelikefalin 0.5 mcg/kg IV post-dialysis (κ-opioid receptor agonist) — FDA-approved 2021 · Nemolizumab (IL-31Rα) — investigational for CKD pruritus
systemic-targeted.detail: Difelikefalin (Korsuva): First FDA-approved therapy specifically for CKD-associated pruritus in hemodialysis adults. Peripherally restricted κ-opioid receptor agonist (does not cross BBB); administered IV 3×/week after dialysis. Significantly reduces Worst Itching Intensity NRS vs placebo in KALM-1 and KALM-2 trials. Does not require renal dose adjustment. Main side effects: dizziness, nausea, somnolence. PMID 29385376.

topical.text: Capsaicin 0.075% cream TID-QID (desensitize TRPV1) · High-concentration capsaicin 8% patch (Qutenza, specialist application) · Lidocaine 4% solution or 5% patch · Menthol 1-3% cream (cooling analgesia) · Ice pack test and therapeutic cooling
topical.detail: Capsaicin: Most studied topical for neuropathic itch; initial burning (minutes) followed by TRPV1 desensitization and reduced itch. Must be applied consistently for 4-6 weeks for benefit. High-concentration 8% patch (Qutenza): single 60-minute application by clinician; lasts 3 months. FDA-approved for neuropathic pain; used off-label for neuropathic itch. Lidocaine patches: Applied 12h on/12h off to symptomatic dermatomal area; especially useful for postherpetic itch. PMID 29385376.

systemic-nonimmune.text: Gabapentin 300-3600mg/day (titrate) · Pregabalin 75-300mg/day · Tricyclic antidepressants: amitriptyline 10-75mg QHS or nortriptyline · Duloxetine (SNRI) 60mg QD for SFN · Physical therapy / paraspinal muscle release (notalgia) · Cervical traction / surgery (brachioradial, structural cause)
systemic-nonimmune.detail: Gabapentinoids: First-line systemic for neuropathic itch; alpha-2-delta calcium channel subunit blockade reduces ectopic nerve firing. Titrate slowly; common side effects: dizziness, somnolence, weight gain. TCAs: Amitriptyline for sleep disruption + analgesic effect; nortriptyline better tolerated in elderly (less anticholinergic). Start 10mg QHS, titrate to 50-75mg. Duloxetine: SNRI with evidence in diabetic SFN. PMID 29385376.

systemic-targeted.text: Botulinum toxin A (intradermal injections) for notalgia paresthetica and brachioradial pruritus · NMDA antagonists (memantine) for central sensitization · Nerve block / cervical epidural for structural radiculopathy
systemic-targeted.detail: Botulinum toxin A: Intradermal injections of 50-100 units across affected dermatome; reduces itch for 3-6 months; requires repeat treatment. Evidence from small RCTs and case series in notalgia paresthetica. Nerve blocks: Targeted paravertebral or cervical epidural blocks for confirmed radiculopathy. Interventional pain specialist referral for refractory cases. Surgical decompression: Reserved for confirmed structural cervical stenosis in brachioradial pruritus after failed conservative therapy.

topical.text: Ceramide-rich emollients QD-BID (barrier restoration) · Menthol 1-2% (symptomatic cooling) · Topical calcineurin inhibitors off-label
topical.detail: In idiopathic chronic pruritus (diagnosis of exclusion), barrier restoration with emollients is the foundation. Menthol provides temporary relief. Topical steroids are generally not indicated in the absence of primary skin inflammation.

systemic-nonimmune.text: Gabapentin 300-1800mg/day · Pregabalin 75-150mg/day · Mirtazapine 15-30mg QHS (NK1 + H1 + NaSSA) · Doxepin 10-25mg QHS (potent H1/H2 antihistamine) · Aprepitant 80mg QD (NK1 receptor antagonist) · Low-dose naltrexone 1.5-4.5mg QHS
systemic-nonimmune.detail: Mirtazapine: NaSSA antidepressant; potent H1 and NK1 receptor antagonism; excellent for nocturnal pruritus; start 15mg QHS (weight gain, sedation are common side effects). Doxepin: Potent H1 + H2 + muscarinic antagonist at low doses; 10-25mg QHS; avoid in elderly (anticholinergic burden). Aprepitant: NK1 receptor antagonist (antiemetic drug); off-label; evidence in cancer-related, chronic renal, and idiopathic pruritus. Low-dose naltrexone: Emerging evidence in pruritus; immunomodulatory at 1.5-4.5mg (different mechanism from standard 50mg dose). PMID 29385376.

systemic-targeted.text: Nemolizumab (IL-31Rα mAb) — approved for prurigo nodularis (2023); emerging evidence in chronic pruritus · Dupilumab off-label if atopic background suspected · Aprepitant (NK1R) — used in cancer-related and chronic pruritus
systemic-targeted.detail: Nemolizumab: IL-31 receptor α-chain blocking antibody; IL-31 is a key pruritogen driving itch and prurigo nodularis. FDA-approved for prurigo nodularis (age ≥12) in 2023; off-label for idiopathic chronic itch. SQ Q4W. Dupilumab: Off-label for chronic pruritus without AD; may be effective when atopic background or type 2 inflammation suspected but not formally diagnosed. Caution: use evidence-based indications; document atopic features before prescribing. PMID 29385376.
